the_bottleneck.named_by_the_benchmark: OSWorld 2.1, 108 long-horizon workflows, >250 agent steps, names constraint tracking and mid-task change detection as the failure modes
the_bottleneck.named_by_this_project: Five thousand documents change nothing, because the search cannot say 'closer' -- 'the search has no measure of distance to the part it is trying to reach'
the_bottleneck.measured_here: asked to mark one item complete and leave two alone, the two-action organ scored every candidate 2.0 and ranked 'Toggle All Input' first -- a control that would complete all three and violate the constraint while satisfying the named one. A goal that is a list of strings cannot express 'and not the others'.

the_idea.one_line: a postcondition is not a string; it is a clause matrix with polarity and scope, and a candidate action is scored by how many clauses it changes
clauses: INVARIANT: gamma keeps the state it has now
the_idea.why_it_generalises: nothing here knows what a todo is. A row is a container that declares a text and holds a control; a control with no name is addressed by the text of the row it sits in, which is where a person looks too. The app supplies every word.

benchmark.family: TodoMVC, 11 self-contained implementations in 11 frameworks, none written here

T1_one_of_three.task: mark beta complete but leave alpha and gamma uncompleted

T2_two_of_four.task: mark alpha and beta complete but leave gamma and delta uncompleted

T3_mid_task_change.task: mark alpha and beta complete, then the user completes alpha as well; the run must detect the drift and report it

the_control_that_gives_the_result_meanin.procedure: a loop with no constraint does the cheapest thing available: the global toggle (Mark all as complete / Toggle All Input / Mark all todos as complete).
the_control_that_gives_the_result_meanin.what_it_measured: on 6 apps the global toggle completed the two protected rows; on 5 it completed nothing at all. Either way the task is not done, and the constraint organ is 11/11 on the same 11 apps.
the_control_that_gives_the_result_meanin.honest_note: the control is deliberately the strongest cheap action a constraint-blind loop would take, not a strawman: a global toggle is one click and is exactly what the two-action organ ranked first.

bugs_found_by_running.bug: polarity by adjacency instead of scope
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: 'leave alpha and gamma uncompleted' classified alpha as a weak INVARIANT, so the loop checked alpha 12 times and never reached the positive clause
bugs_found_by_running.fix: a leave/keep scope runs to the end of its list, and a negative is strictly stronger than an invariant, so the strong reading wins

bugs_found_by_running.bug: the leave scope ran past a contrastive conjunction
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: 'leave alpha alone but mark beta complete' made beta NEGATIVE too, inverting the task's own instruction

bugs_found_by_running.bug: a satisfied clause was scored like an open one
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: every named row scored 6.0, so acting on the protected row looked as good as acting on the open one
bugs_found_by_running.fix: a clause that already holds scores negative -- acting on it can only break it

bugs_found_by_running.bug: row membership paired two traversals by index
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: row_text was None on every control, so no row-addressed action was possible on the two shadow-DOM apps
bugs_found_by_running.fix: stamp the row text on the element BEFORE the element list is read, and carry the row text itself rather than a sequence number

bugs_found_by_running.bug: clause items matched by equality against the whole row text
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: 'Toggle Todo beta' never equalled 'beta', so every row scored 0.0 and the planner fell through to a global checkbox
bugs_found_by_running.fix: match the item as a WORD inside what the row publishes, on both the state reader and the scorer

bugs_found_by_running.bug: the row container was assumed to be a listitem
bugs_found_by_running.symptom: a 10 s timeout clicking a row on one implementation
bugs_found_by_running.fix: try listitem, then row, then the plain tags, then refuse by name

honest_limits: Still 11 apps of ONE specification, three tasks, one host, one browser build, no repeat trials. This is depth within a family, not generalisation across families.
Three to six actions, not 250. The tasks chain create -> mutate -> verify, but nothing here approaches OSWorld's horizon and no OSWorld task was run.

The clause reader is a closed word class (complete/incomplete/leave/keep/but). A task phrased outside it yields no clause or the wrong polarity. It is a parser of a small grammar, not an understanding of the instruction.
The postcondition is read from the app's own declaration, so an app that declares the wrong state would be believed. The effect is only as trustworthy as the declaration.
The control is one procedure, not a search over adversarial policies. A blind loop that happened to click the right row would have passed, and nothing here rules that out.
The SWE-bench generation gap (1.4% ceiling against 78.80%) is untouched.

tests.no_browser_needed: the clause reader and the scorer are pure functions of what the interface declared
